{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABYf9ipw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhCETnk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 7, "title": "Make a legally redistributable Sega Saturn homebrew game playable in the browser", "body": "## Problem

The deployed GitHub Pages build is currently a **CPU bootstrap/debugger**, not a playable Sega Saturn emulator. [Issue #3](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/issues/3) / [PR #4](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/4) implemented a small original SH-2 interpreter, RAM/BIOS mapping, and a six-instruction homebrew fixture. [Issue #5](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/issues/5) / [PR #6](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/6) added GitHub Pages deployment. There is **no game/disc loader, frame-based video output, real input device model, or playable software** yet.

We need a meaningful **first end-to-end, browser-playable Saturn homebrew game**, with a testable and legally redistributable demonstration that needs no proprietary Sega BIOS. This is a substantial compatibility milestone, **not** a request to claim that commercial games or all Saturn hardware now work.

## Expected outcome

A visitor to **https://takahirox.github.io/saturn-rust/** can select a clearly licensed **Sega Saturn-targeted homebrew disc image**, or load their own authorized compatible image from a local file, choose the **BIOS-less HLE** path, start the program, view graphics, control gameplay using a keyboard (and optionally Gamepad API), and reach an observable game state such as scoring, success/failure and restart.

**The game must run as guest SH-2 instructions through our Rust emulator and emulated Saturn devices.** It must not be a JavaScript/Canvas remake, a hardcoded screen animation, a native host game engine, a special-case replacement of the game loop, or a raw instruction fixture misleadingly advertised as a game ROM. Optimize later; correct execution and playable functionality come first.

The external **user-provided BIOS** mode must remain available and private. State its *actual* compatibility honestly: this Issue requires successful play through HLE first; native Sega BIOS booting requires additional low-level hardware and may remain a separate milestone. Do not silently redirect a user-selected BIOS boot into HLE and claim real-BIOS compatibility.

## Context and reproduction

- New functionality: reproduction steps are not applicable. Inspect current `main` before implementation, including `src/cpu.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/wasm.rs`, `web/`, `scripts/build-web.sh`, the Playwright tests, [architecture](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/architecture.md), and [setup](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/setup.md).
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [the Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md). Author Issue/PR text, docs and commits in **English**. Keep the smallest coherent implementation that meets the acceptance criteria, even if the feature needs several focused PRs; **do not close this Issue on partial progress**.
- Saturn is **CD-based**, so use terms such as homebrew **disc image (ISO or BIN/CUE)** rather than implying Saturn commercial games are ordinary cartridge ROMs. Any temporary SH-2 executable-loading helper must be accurately labelled and cannot substitute for the required disc-image demonstration.
- The emulator's CPU, memory system, BIOS HLE, video, input, disc handling and scheduler must remain **independently implemented in Rust** from hardware/programming manuals. No third-party emulator/CPU/peripheral cores; ordinary Wasm/browser infrastructure libraries and separately built homebrew development tools are not emulator-core reuse. No source/code copying or transliteration from reference emulators.
- Consult [Saturn hardware/boot manuals](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs), notably the SH-2 programming and SH7604 hardware manuals, Saturn Overview, VDP1/VDP2, SCU, SMPC, CD block and Boot ROM manuals. Record hardware-address and register references next to implemented behavior and identify approximations.

### Legally usable game candidates and fallback

Investigate candidates **before including assets in this repository or hosting them on Pages**:

1. [slinga-homebrew/Disasteroids](https://github.com/slinga-homebrew/Disasteroids): playable Saturn Asteroids-style homebrew; repository has an **MIT LICENSE for its software** and an ISO release, but it also includes music WAVs/other assets and uses Jo Engine. **Do not assume that the MIT software license clears each bundled recording, all assets, linked SDK components, or an already-built disc image.** Audit individual rights and distribution terms; use as an *optional longer-term compatibility target*, not mandatory for the first playable game.
2. [buhman/saturn-examples](https://github.com/buhman/saturn-examples): MIT-licensed Saturn examples, including a `wordle/` program. Assess dependency, game assets/word list and build/redistribution rights independently; no release image was confirmed.
3. [johannes-fetz/joengine](https://github.com/johannes-fetz/joengine): MIT-licensed game-development engine, **not** itself a redistributable game image, and it does not establish the rights of each game or all third-party Sega SDK assets.

Prefer an independently verifiable, genuinely redistributable, manageable Saturn homebrew target if one can be confirmed. **If no complete game's source + disc image + assets + toolchain provenance can be cleared, author a tiny original Saturn-targeted game** with original visuals (and optional original sound) and publish its *buildable guest source plus generated disc image* with an explicit permission/license for every distributed component. Do not automatically download/republish third-party binaries of uncertain status, assume "free download" means redistribution permission, or include proprietary Sega BIOS/IP binaries. A self-authored mini-game is an **acceptable and preferred safe fallback** and can keep this Issue achievable without external permission delays. Do not add a blanket project-wide license without the repository owner's authorization; explicitly license the new game's files/assets and describe any external build dependencies.

## Functional implementation scope

### 1. Select and define one small real guest game

- Before expanding peripheral emulation, select a **minimal playable target** requiring the smallest documented subset of Saturn hardware; write down how it boots and which SH-2 instructions, registers and devices its binary uses. If implementing the original fallback, a simple interactive **collect/dodge, Pong, or Snake-like** game is appropriate.
- Minimum gameplay contract: rendered playfield and moving player or cursor, input that changes guest game state visibly, scoring/progress feedback, at least one win/loss or completion condition, and ability to restart **inside the emulated program**. Keep guest game logic in Saturn-targeted code, not host JS.
- Produce a reproducible, Saturn-appropriate build of the guest program and a disc image with documented filesystem/boot layout; demonstrate that it is a genuine SH-2/Saturn-targeted executable rather than a bespoke JS app. If an external cross-compiler/assembler is needed **only to build the homebrew game**, document its provenance and license separately from the Rust emulator.

### 2. Boot and load a real disc image

- Add a browser-local disc picker for **at least one documented Saturn-compatible disc-image format** suitable for the chosen game (ISO 2048-sector, or BIN/CUE if required by the target). Reject invalid/truncated/unsupported formats and sizes with useful error messages. Support the **actual format of the sample playable game**; list other formats as future compatibility work rather than accepting files that are not properly parsed.
- Provide a BIOS-less HLE **boot path** that reads the chosen disc image's documented Saturn boot metadata, locates/loads the guest executable to documented emulated memory, initializes the correct SH-2 state and runs its actual instructions. Build the minimum HLE bootstrap needed for this homebrew and document unsupported full BIOS services. Do **not** silently load arbitrary bytes and call them a disc boot.
- Respect high/low work RAM, endianness, valid memory access, reset, relevant MMIO and any necessary CD data-read abstractions. If the guest performs runtime disc reads, implement the documented minimum CD block behavior it needs (or pick a self-contained first game that requires none after startup). No network upload, CDN or persistent browser storage of user-provided files.
- Maintain external BIOS upload selection and accurate errors/limitations; the user can choose it, but successful Sega BIOS boot/game compatibility is not a pre-merge condition for this HLE-first milestone.

### 3. Emulate the minimal devices for *actual* playable behavior

- Extend the SH-2 interpreter with the verified instruction, flag, exception/interrupt, addressing and delay-slot behavior **used by the chosen guest**, with tests derived from manuals and deterministic traces. Preserve the existing baseline tests. No imported SH-2 CPU core.
- Implement the **specific video path the game actually uses** (e.g. documented VDP2 display/VRAM/CRAM/tile or bitmap subset, or VDP1 command rendering if essential) in Rust. Expose a framebuffer to Canvas; make clear that unsupported VDP modes remain unsupported. Do not draw game elements directly from game state in JS.
- Emulate the necessary Saturn **SMPC/port input behavior** and bridge keyboard arrows/actions/start; map input into the guest via emulated hardware reads, never by directly modifying the game's registers/memory or host-renderer state. A gamepad mapping is desirable if it can be implemented without harming the baseline, but keyboard alone is mandatory.
- Implement **deterministic frame/update stepping** with sufficient device/CPU scheduling for the selected game, not an unconstrained CPU loop blocking the UI. Use a single-threaded correctness reference first; Web Workers, native-code JIT, dynamic recompilation, perfect audiovisual timing, and broad game compatibility are future work.
- Only add audio/SCSP/68EC000 support if the selected game's functional playability truly requires it. If sound is not supported, label the build as silent and record that limitation.

### 4. Browser, distribution and tests

- Extend the existing WebAssembly and static browser frontend, keeping it deployable by [Browser Pages](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/.github/workflows/pages.yml). Provide a prominent **Play Homebrew** path using a safely distributable packaged sample or a locally generated/source-built image as licensing allows, and also support local image selection.
- Display graphics, provide keyboard instructions, Run/Pause/Reset or Start/Restart as appropriate, and show actionable unsupported-hardware and boot errors. Do not regress the existing SH-2 debugger / BIOS controls.
- Use a deterministic headless/automated game-play test: boot the actual image through the same Wasm/HLE path as the UI; advance emulated frames; simulate at least two distinct input sequences; assert **guest-derived state** and visible frame-buffer/pixel differences, score/progress and restart. This must detect a no-op controller, a static pre-rendered screenshot, and a guest CPU that does not execute.
- Validate documented local build commands, Rust native tests, Wasm build, Playwright smoke tests, and existing Pages-path handling. Tests must use only cleared/original assets, not a Sega BIOS or commercial game.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least **one actual Sega Saturn-targeted homebrew game** can be loaded as a documented disc-image format and played in the existing browser app, **without a proprietary BIOS**, with player input, graphics, observable score/progress, terminal/win/loss condition and in-game restart.
- [ ] The game runs as emulated guest SH-2 code. Its graphical output originates from emulated VDP memory/register behavior and input arrives through a guest-visible emulated input interface. No substituted JavaScript game logic or canned frame sequence.
- [ ] The chosen game, every included asset, packaged disc image, and all copied dependencies have **documented redistributable licenses/permissions** and attributions. If candidates cannot be cleared, an original licensed game + reproducible build and disc image replaces them; no unknown-license release assets, Sega firmware or commercial games are committed/hosted.
- [ ] Disc parsing, HLE boot/load, CPU behavior, memory/device mapping, rendering and input each have tests for representative successful and error cases, with exact supported functionality and known limitations documented. External BIOS mode remains usable as before.
- [ ] The browser accepts a user-supplied supported local disc image without transmitting it, rejects unsupported/malformed data with useful feedback, and can run the licensed demo via a documented Play action. The UI clearly distinguishes HLE playability from incomplete real-BIOS support.
- [ ] Automated native and Wasm/browser checks prove that controls affect **guest state**, frames visibly change, the game can be progressed and restarted, and the result is not just the original six-instruction fixture. Tests run on a browser URL rooted at `/saturn-rust/`.
- [ ] The existing GitHub Pages workflow can build/test/deploy the playable static site using only public/cleared assets. README and architecture docs accurately explain build steps, how to play, input mappings, license/provenance, current supported game(s), and remaining subsystem/compatibility gaps.
- [ ] No prebuilt emulator cores, speculative dynarec/worker optimization, external server backend, unrelated UI framework migration, or undocumented proprietary SDK binary is introduced. The PR honestly reports validations run and any failures/skips.

## Optional validation

- Check the original homebrew disc and input behavior against a separately installed reference Saturn emulator, without copying its implementation or bundling its firmware.
- Expand controller support with the browser Gamepad API, add original sound effects, or measure baseline FPS once accurate gameplay exists. These are **not** mandatory for this first playable milestone.
- Test additional openly licensed homebrew titles **only after auditing all source, images, audio, code dependencies and distribution rights**. In particular, Disasteroids is an interesting *future* target but its licensing and larger device requirements are not automatically satisfied by the MIT repository badge.

## Required post-merge verification

- After GitHub Pages deploys the merged `main` revision, verify the **live** page at https://takahirox.github.io/saturn-rust/ loads the licensed homebrew, displays graphics, accepts input, updates the score/progress, reaches a terminal state and restarts. This publishing check can **only** be completed post-merge and must not be a pre-merge approval condition.
- Record the published revision, successful deployment and any production-only defects. Do not claim production playability from a green pre-merge smoke test alone.
